sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Interstellar objects, such as the recently observed ‘Oumuamua, are celestial bodies that originate outside the solar system and pass through it on hyperbolic trajectories. Unlike asteroids and comets bound to the Sun, these objects are not gravitationally tethered, offering a rare opportunity to study material from distant star systems. Their unusual trajectories, shapes, and compositions challenge existing models of planetary formation and interstellar dynamics. Observations suggest that some interstellar objects may carry organic compounds, raising questions about the distribution of prebiotic material in the galaxy. Detection is complicated by their high velocity, small size, and transient visibility. As observational technology improves, astronomers anticipate more frequent identification, potentially providing unprecedented insights into the conditions and processes of exoplanetary systems. Studying such objects may inform theories about the origin of life and the broader dynamics of galactic matter distribution.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: Electric vehicles (EVs) are often heralded as environmentally friendly alternatives to traditional internal combustion vehicles. They reduce tailpipe emissions, contributing to cleaner urban air and lower greenhouse gas output. However, their overall sustainability depends on the source of electricity and the lifecycle of batteries. Manufacturing batteries requires extraction of rare earth minerals, often obtained through ecologically damaging practices. Recycling and disposal of batteries pose additional environmental challenges. Charging infrastructure remains limited in many regions, impeding widespread adoption. Furthermore, EVs may shift environmental burdens rather than eliminate them entirely, as electricity generation is often still fossil-fuel based. Policymakers must consider energy policies, supply chains, and urban planning to make EV adoption genuinely sustainable. Consequently, EVs should be viewed as transitional instruments within a broader framework of energy reform, rather than ultimate solutions to environmental problems.

questions.q: The passage primarily discusses interstellar objects as
opts: common features of the solar system
key sources for understanding distant planetary systems
questions.why: They offer “a rare opportunity to study material from distant star systems”. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Under Secretary, Legislative Affairs), Feb 2026.

questions.q: The term “hyperbolic trajectories” implies that interstellar objects
opts: orbit the Sun in closed paths
move too fast to be captured by the Sun
questions.why: They are “not gravitationally tethered”; a hyperbola is an open path. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Under Secretary, Legislative Affairs), Feb 2026.

questions.q: Why are interstellar objects difficult to observe?
opts: They are small, fast and visible only briefly
questions.why: Fifth sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Under Secretary, Legislative Affairs), Feb 2026.

questions.q: The presence of organic compounds in interstellar objects suggests
opts: prebiotic materials may be widespread in the galaxy
they cannot enter the solar system
questions.why: Fourth sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Under Secretary, Legislative Affairs), Feb 2026.

questions.q: The overall tone of the passage is
questions.why: It reports observations and their implications. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Under Secretary, Legislative Affairs), Feb 2026.

questions.q: The environmental benefits of EVs primarily depend on
questions.why: Third sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Lecturer in Mathematics), Sep 2026.

questions.q: Which major environmental concern related to EVs does the passage highlight?
questions.why: Fourth sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Lecturer in Mathematics), Sep 2026.

questions.q: Why does the author describe EVs as “transitional instruments”?
opts: They are interim solutions on the way to wider reform
questions.why: They are part of “a broader framework of energy reform, rather than ultimate solutions”. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Lecturer in Mathematics), Sep 2026.

questions.q: Which factor most limits widespread EV adoption according to the passage?
questions.why: Sixth sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Lecturer in Mathematics), Sep 2026.

questions.why: Benefits are acknowledged, with clear limits. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Lecturer in Mathematics), Sep 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “I ____ him for ten years.”
questions.why: Action continuing to now with a period: present perfect. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, “The earth moves round the sun.”
opts: The teacher said that the earth moves round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth moved round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth had moved round the sun.
The teacher told the earth moves round the sun.
questions.why: Universal truths keep the present tense. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “transparent”:
questions.why: Opaque lets no light through. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “He is senior ____ me by two years.”
questions.why: Senior, junior, superior and inferior take 'to'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “a bolt from the blue”:
opts: good news expected for a long time
questions.why: Standard idiom. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: 'Annapoorni Super Six', a 2026 LPG scheme, was launched by:
Which amendment reserved one-third of seats in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies for women?
questions.why: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam.

questions.q: Suchika Tariyal won India's first-ever Asian Games medal in which sport (2026)?
questions.why: Bronze in the 60 kg class.

questions.q: Which state was formed on 1 November 2000?
questions.why: Uttarakhand followed on 9 November and Jharkhand on 15 November 2000.

questions.q: Who is Goa's Minister for Information Technology, who announced the Goa AI Policy 2026?
DRDO's High Altitude Platform System (HAPS) airship reached an altitude of about ___ in a flight trial (Oct 2026).
Which company received approval in October 2026 to acquire a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank?
The National Biodiversity Authority, which disbursed Access and Benefit Sharing funds in 2026, is headquartered in:
questions.why: Set up under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.

questions.q: Luke J. Lindberg of the USA was appointed Executive Director of the:
Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet'?
questions.why: India's Mangalyaan reached Mars orbit in 2014.

questions.q: Two trains move in opposite directions at 60 km/h and 90 km/h. Their lengths are 1.10 km and 0.9 km. How many seconds does the slower train take to cross the faster?
questions.why: 2000 m at 150 km/h (125/3 m/s) = 48 s. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: Statement: Should a legally enforceable 'Right to Disconnect' ban companies from contacting employees outside working hours? Arguments: I. Yes. Constant availability causes burnout, harms mental health and lowers long-term productivity. II. No. In a global economy across time zones, a rigid ban will hurt competitiveness and growth.
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.why: Both give a serious, relevant reason. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: Peter and Beckon walk in the same direction. Peter's speed is 5 km/h and Beckon's 6 km/h. If Peter starts 3 km behind Beckon, after how many hours will they be 17 km apart?
questions.why: The gap grows by 1 km/h, from 3 to 17: 14 hours. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: A ₹20,00,000 portfolio loses 20% a year, compounded. At the end of year 2, after that year's loss, ₹25,000 is added. What is the value right after the injection?
Three partners shared profit in the ratio 5 : 7 : 8, having invested for 14, 8 and 7 months. What was the ratio of their investments?
questions.why: Investment ∝ profit ÷ time: 5/14 : 7/8 : 8/7, × 56 = 20 : 49 : 64. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: Statements: All lions are tigers. No tiger is a dog. All dogs are cats. Conclusions: I. All lions are cats. II. Some cats are tigers.
questions.why: Lions and tigers have no link to cats; the cats that are dogs cannot be tigers, and nothing else is known. GPSC CBRT, Apr 2024.

questions.q: Six books (English, Hindi, Science, Computer, Maths, Sanskrit) have different page counts. Computer has fewer pages than only two books. English has more than Science but fewer than Sanskrit. Science is not the least. Sanskrit has fewer than Hindi. The third-lowest book has 28 pages. Sanskrit + Computer = 89 and Computer + English = 63. How many pages does Sanskrit have?
questions.why: Order: Hindi > Sanskrit > Computer > English (28) > Science > Maths. Computer = 35, Sanskrit = 54. GPSC CBRT, Apr 2024.

questions.q: Eight friends P, Q, R, S, T, U, V, W stand in a line facing north. R and W are immediate neighbours of S. V is an immediate neighbour of U and W. T and Q are immediate neighbours of P. Neither T nor R is at an end. U is to the right of T. Who is second to the left of W?
questions.why: Line: Q P T R S W V U. Second left of W is R. GPSC CBRT, Apr 2024.

questions.q: What is the third letter of the meaningful word formed from the 1st, 3rd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 9th letters of ASTRONAUT?
questions.why: Letters A, T, R, N, U, T make TRUANT. GPSC CBRT, Apr 2024.

questions.q: Complete the series: 7, 13, 25, 45, 75, ?
questions.why: Differences 6, 12, 20, 30, 42 (n(n + 1)): 75 + 42 = 117. GPSC CBRT, Apr 2024.

questions.q: Hahnemann's 'Chronic Diseases' second edition was published in five volumes between:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. The first edition appeared in 1828–1830.

questions.q: The word 'dynamis' in homoeopathic philosophy refers to:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. The spirit-like power animating the body.

questions.q: According to Hahnemann, the most important part of treatment in an epidemic is to:
opts: use the same remedy as the last epidemic
study many cases to find the genus epidemicus
treat each case only with mother tinctures
wait for the epidemic to pass
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §100–102.

questions.q: Effects of mental strain and overwork in students, with brain fag, headache and weak memory, suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Both suit nervous exhaustion from study.

questions.q: Arterial congestion with a slow pulse, a red streak down the middle of the tongue and convulsions, as in eclampsia, suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Veratrum viride: red streak on the tongue, violent congestion.

questions.q: Remedies are said to be 'complementary' when:
opts: one completes the action of the other
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Example: Calcarea and Belladonna; Sulphur and Aloe.

questions.q: Desire to be magnetised, sympathetic nature, fear of thunderstorms and of being alone, and burning pains point to:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Phosphorus: wants company and sympathy.

questions.q: Mother tinctures in the HPI are prepared mainly by:
opts: maceration or percolation of the drug in alcohol
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Trituration is for insoluble drugs; succussion makes liquid potencies.

questions.q: The HPI standard for a homoeopathic drug lays down its:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Pharmacopoeial monographs fix identity, purity and strength.

questions.q: The repertory with chapters in the order Mind, Vertigo, Head and so on, following Hahnemann's schema, is:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Hahnemannian anatomical schema from head to foot.

questions.q: The term 'grading' in a repertory refers to:
opts: the value assigned to a remedy in a rubric, shown by typeface
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Shows how strongly the remedy produced the symptom.

questions.q: A sudden rise in blood pressure is corrected within seconds mainly by the:
opts: Baroreceptor reflex from the carotid sinus and aortic arch
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Baroreceptors buffer short-term changes; the kidneys set long-term pressure.

questions.q: The normal total leucocyte count in adults is:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Raised in infection, low in typhoid and dengue.

questions.q: Haematuria, proteinuria, oedema and hypertension after a sore throat in a child suggest:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. One to three weeks after a streptococcal infection.

questions.q: On abdominal ultrasonography, a gallstone appears as:
opts: an echogenic (bright) focus with posterior acoustic shadowing that moves with posture
a solid mass in the liver
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Echogenic focus + acoustic shadow + mobility = gallstone.

questions.q: Pain in the upper abdomen going through to the back, with very high serum amylase, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Gallstones and alcohol are the main causes.

questions.q: Allergic rhinitis with violent sneezing, and itching of the palate, worse from the smell of flowers, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Sabadilla: hay fever.

questions.q: Sciatica with cramping pain, worse on the left, relieved by heat and pressure, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Colocynth: cramping pains, better pressure.

questions.q: The ovarian hormone that maintains the endometrium in the second half of the cycle is:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. From the corpus luteum.

questions.q: A newborn's Apgar score is assessed at:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Heart rate, breathing, tone, reflex, colour.

questions.q: Burns of the face and neck are dangerous mainly because of:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Early airway assessment is vital.

questions.q: A painful red lump at the eyelid margin is called a:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. A chalazion is usually painless.

questions.q: The 'Mission Indradhanush' programme aims to:
opts: raise full immunisation coverage of children and pregnant women
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Launched in 2014.

questions.q: The poison that causes garlic odour of breath and 'rice-water' stools resembling cholera is:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Acute arsenic poisoning.

questions.q: A doctor's duty under the law to inform the police applies to:
opts: medicolegal cases such as injuries, poisoning and suspicious deaths
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. MLC registration and intimation.
